articles.author: Gaby Hinsliff
articles.summary: The government says it can transform the state with AI, but it is no match for the resulting stream of machine-generated slop. And we all pay the cost Another morning, another avalanche of emails. Even after a guilty cull, my inbox is sitting at well over 7,000, but lately I’ve started subscribing to the Quentin Crisp theory of housework: why bother, when after four years or so you stop noticing the accumulating dust? Empty inboxes just fill up again anyway. In theory, email was supposed to save hours of meetings, phone calls and standing over photocopiers. Instead, we just spend hours deleting stuff people wouldn’t have bothered telling us if it had meant picking up the phone, but which they can now spam to their entire database at the click of a button. The glorious ease and convenience of being able to reach the world in seconds came, we now know, with the inconvenience of them being able to reach you right back. Mitchell Fairbarn, 34, took the Chilean flamingo, Peachy, from the Flamingo Las Vegas wildlife habitat in March and carried the bird to his hotel room by its neck. Animal experts told the court Peachy suffered torn feathers and blood loss. A state veterinarian said the bird has largely recovered but is now more anxious around people. stories.summary: Elon Musk ordered the Starlink slowdown that hindered Kyiv’s defense last week, US officials told The Wall Street Journal, an episode that punctuated a stunning breakdown in US-Ukraine ties. Kyiv said Tuesday that Washington had resumed intelligence sharing , which had become another point of contention, along with the US’ diesel deal with Moscow and waiving of Russia sanctions. This “ staggering one-two punch ” to Ukraine could be because US President Donald Trump needed a “scapegoat” for high fuel prices, an Atlantic correspondent argued. The reasons for Ukrainian leaders ’ criticism of Trump are less ambiguous: They believe Trump has “gone so far in putting Russia’s interests ahead of Ukraine’s security that holding their tongue would be riskier than speaking up,” The New York Times reported. — Brendan Ruberry
